//: The deny list is a speed bump plus a second layer, not a boundary. Claude Code's own docs warn that Bash permission patterns constraining command arguments are fragile - flag placement and variable use route around them (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions, read 2026-08-23). Its value is that deny is evaluated before allow, so these rules also constrain the broad Bash(git:*) below, and that the matcher is shell-aware where a grep is not. The mechanical backstop for WORKER sessions is hooks/worker-git-guardrail.sh; this block is the only mechanical guard shepherd's own session has. The operations named here are the ones CLAUDE.md already forbids by instruction (S2 rule 10: never git add -A, never git commit -a) plus the destructive git of S4. One rule is deliberately exact rather than wildcarded: `Bash(git add .)` names the whole-tree add, because `Bash(git add .*)` also blocks every dot-prefixed path - `git add .claude/settings.json`, `git add .gitignore` - which is routine, safe work. Deny beats allow with no exceptions, so an over-broad rule here has no escape hatch.
